content.title: About
content.content: The Big Mac is McDonald's signature double‑burger, made of two beef patties, special sauce, lettuce, cheese, pickles and onions, all stacked between three sesame seed buns.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Big Mac was first introduced in 1967 in Pittsburgh.
Its famous tagline “Two all‑beef patties, special sauce, lettuce, cheese, pickles, onions on a sesame seed bun” is known worldwide.
In 1975 the Big Mac Index was created by The Economist as a simple way to compare purchasing power parity across countries.
The Big Mac arrived in Russia in the early 1990s and quickly became a menu staple.
A vegetarian version called the Veggie Mac replaces the beef patties with plant‑based patties.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The two beef patties provide roughly 25 g of high‑quality protein, essential for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is readily absorbed and supports oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The slice of cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and the bun contribute B12, B6 and niacin, which help with energy metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Lettuce and pickles contribute a modest amount of fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A single Big Mac contains about 540 kcal, which can contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: The sandwich is rich in saturated fats and salt, which may increase cardiovascular risk when consumed in excess.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: It contains gluten (bun), dairy (cheese) and soy (in the special sauce), which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some ingredients include additives that may not be suitable for people with sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The Big Mac is typically served in its branded wrapper. Eat it by hand, optionally splitting it in half, and pair it with fries and a drink. For a lighter option, some replace the regular bun with a whole‑grain version.

content.title: Storage
content.content: If not eaten immediately, store the Big Mac in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, reheat in a microwave or oven to restore the bun’s texture.
